title: Move the ownership check into PostPolicy
summary: Pull the duplicated 403 check out of update and destroy into a policy, and trip over the empty base controller of Laravel 11 and later.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Http\Requests\UpdatePostRequest;
use App\Models\Post;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class PostController extends Controller
{
    public function update(UpdatePostRequest $request, Post $post)
    {
        if ($request->user()->id !== $post->user_id && ! $request->user()->is_admin) {
            abort(403);
        }

        $post->update($request->validated());

        return redirect()->route('posts.show', $post);
    }

    public function destroy(Request $request, Post $post)
    {
        if ($request->user()->id !== $post->user_id && ! $request->user()->is_admin) {
            abort(403);
        }

        $post->delete();

        return redirect()->route('posts.index');
    }
}

turns.user: update and destroy in PostController have the same if + abort(403). move it into a policy. laravel 12

assistant.body: Sure! Let's put the decision in PostPolicy, a single source of truth for who may touch a post. Laravel discovers a policy in app/Policies by the model name, so nothing needs registering.
The stub comes with seven methods, viewAny through forceDelete. Only two are needed. Note: the controller action is destroy, but the policy ability is delete.

Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. Since Laravel 11 the base Controller in a new app is an empty abstract class, and the AuthorizesRequests trait that provides authorize() is not on it. I wrote it the Laravel 10 way.
There are two fixes. Call Gate::authorize() instead, or put the trait back on the base class. The second keeps every controller written the same way, so I recommend it.

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\Access\AuthorizesRequests;

abstract class Controller
{
    use AuthorizesRequests;
}

turns.user: also admins shouldn't be able to delete other people's posts. we had an incident. editing stays as is

assistant.body: Only delete loses the is_admin check. update is untouched, so admins can still edit anyone's post.
